equity.name: Equity
equity.short: Your share of the pot if the hand were played to the end.
equity.long: The share of the pot you win on average once all cards are dealt. 60% equity means 60 of every 100 chips in the pot, on average.

range.name: Range
range.short: Every hand an opponent could hold given their actions.
range.long: The set of hands an opponent could have given their position, actions and bet sizes. Your decisions are judged against the range, not their real cards, because that is what you could know.

potOdds.name: Pot odds
potOdds.short: The equity a call needs to break even.
potOdds.long: The bet you have to call divided by the pot after your call. Calling 50 into what becomes a 200 pot needs at least 25% equity.

ev.name: EV (expected value)
ev.short: How many chips an action wins on average.
ev.long: The average result of an action if the same spot repeated many times. Folding counts as zero; calls and raises are compared with it.

evLoss.name: EV loss
evLoss.short: What a decision cost compared with the best one, in bb.
evLoss.long: The gap between the best option's EV and your choice's EV, in big blinds. The verdict is based on it.

foldEquity.name: Fold equity
foldEquity.short: The extra value of opponents folding.
foldEquity.long: The part of a bet's or raise's value that comes from opponents folding. The analysis estimates it, so bet and raise EVs are marked as estimates.

accuracy.name: Accuracy
accuracy.short: Share of decisions rated best or good.
accuracy.long: The share of your decisions that lost at most 0.3 bb compared with the best option.

bb.name: bb (big blind)
bb.long: Wins and losses are measured in big blinds so they compare across stakes.

bb100.name: bb/100
bb100.long: The headline win rate: how many big blinds you win on average every 100 hands.

vpip.name: VPIP
vpip.short: How often you voluntarily put chips in preflop.
vpip.long: The share of hands where you called or raised before the flop (blinds don't count). A high VPIP means playing too many weak hands.

pfr.name: PFR
pfr.long: The share of hands with a preflop raise. The closer PFR is to VPIP, the more aggressively you enter pots.

af.name: AF (aggression factor)
af.short: Postflop bets and raises divided by calls.
af.long: Aggressive actions (bet, raise) divided by calls after the flop. Below 1 points to passive play.

wtsd.name: WTSD
wtsd.short: How often you reach showdown after seeing the flop.
wtsd.long: The share of hands where you saw the flop and went to showdown. A high value often means not letting go of weak hands.

wsd.name: W$SD
wsd.short: How often you win at showdown.
wsd.long: The share of showdowns where you received chips.

allInEv.name: All-in EV
allInEv.short: Expected result of an all-in versus the actual one.
allInEv.long: Once your chips are in with cards to come, only luck decides. All-in EV is what you should win on average, separating luck from decision quality.

kicker.name: Kicker
kicker.short: The side card that breaks a tie.
kicker.long: A card outside the hand itself that decides between equal hands. A pair of aces with a king beats a pair of aces with a queen.

sidePot.name: Side pot
sidePot.short: A separate pot a shorter all-in stack cannot win.
sidePot.long: When a player is all-in for less, bets above their contribution form a separate pot contested only by those who put in more.

splitPot.name: Split pot
splitPot.long: If the best hands are equal the pot is split; an odd chip goes to the first player left of the button.

badBeat.name: Bad beat
badBeat.short: A clear favourite lost to the last cards.
badBeat.long: A player with a big edge (70%+ equity) loses to later cards. That is bad luck, not a mistake.

suckOut.name: Suck-out
suckOut.short: A clear underdog won on the last cards.
suckOut.long: The opposite of a bad beat: a player with a small chance (30% or less) wins thanks to later cards.

verdicts.name: Verdicts
verdicts.long: A decision rated by its EV loss: best is the optimal option; good up to 0.3 bb; inaccuracy up to 1.5 bb; mistake up to 5 bb; blunder over 5 bb.
